test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18th November 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The mean of 15 measurements was calculated to be 50 cm. But it was found that one of the measurements was recorded as 46 cm instead of 61 cm. What is the correct mean (in cm)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Difference of wrong measurements = 61 - 46 = 15 cm

⇒ Mean variation = 15 ÷ 15 = 1 cm

⇒ New mean = 50 + 1 = 51 cm

**∴ Correct mean is 51 cm.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Given:

Total measurements = 15

Initial mean = 50 cm

**Formula used:**

Average / Mean = Sum of observation / Number of observation

Sum of observation = Average x number of observation 

Mean variation = Difference ÷ Total measurements

**Calculation:**

Sum of observation 15 x 50 =750 cm

Difference of wrong measurements = 61 - 46 = 15 cm

New sum of observation = 750 + 15 = 765

Correct mean = 765/15

⇒ 51 cm

∴ Correct mean is 51 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**

If mistaken observation is less than real observation than mean variation = (real observation - mistaken observation)/ Total number of observation and in this condition correct mean is always higher than incorrect mean.

If mistaken observation is more than real observation than mean variation = (mistaken observation - real observation)/ Total number of observation and in this condition correct mean is always less than incorrect mean.
